MECHANISM: TYG's plan permits a participating common stockholder to submit optional cash, currently $100-$5,000 per month. When the fund is at a market premium to NAV at the relevant fixing, the fund issues new common shares directly at the greater of NAV or 95% of market price; when at a discount, the Plan Agent instead buys in the open market. A small participant can therefore receive a bounded direct-issuance discount only in the premium branch.
WHO_PAYS: In the direct-issuance branch, the fund/nonparticipating shareholders bear dilution from issuance below contemporaneous market price but not below the plan formula. In the discount branch there is no issuer concession; the participant bears market purchase price and commissions through the Plan Agent.
WHY_PERSIST: The maximum ordinary optional-cash size is only $5,000 per month, the participant must use the plan and meet operational cutoffs, the branch depends on premium/NAV state, purchase timing is fixed rather than selectable, the issuer may amend/terminate the plan, and exit through the agent carries a fixed transaction fee plus per-share charge. These features make the opportunity operationally annoying and capacity-limited.
CHEAP_DATA_NOW: Primary TYG prospectus text publicly specifies the cash-purchase range, cutoff, premium/discount branch, pricing formula, direct-issuance/open-market distinction and agent-sale charges. Tortoise's public fund page publishes declared distribution/payment dates and later reports NAV/market/DRIP values. A future case can therefore be frozen before its fixing values become public. The current page showed historical 2026 plan outcomes during qualification; those are contamination/calibration only and cannot count as fresh evidence.
CHEAP_EXPRESSION: Prospective upper-bound case using one fixed $5,000 optional cash investment at one predeclared future monthly purchase date. If the direct-issuance premium branch occurs, compare shares received under the frozen max(NAV, 95% market) formula with same-date market value, then apply fixed sale/market frictions. If the open-market branch occurs, the case should not be re-selected or retimed.
FATAL_PROBLEM: This is not a guaranteed 5% arbitrage. If NAV exceeds 95% of market, the discount is smaller than 5%; if the fund is at a discount, the plan uses open-market purchases and the issuer concession disappears. The participant cannot choose the fixing time, must already be a plan participant/stockholder, can face delay and market risk before shares are saleable, and the plan reserves amendment/termination rights. Historical same-issuer plan values are already exposed, so only future OOS events can add evidence.
causal_distinction: This is not the existing CEF dividend-reinvestment expression. The cash source is a participant's optional external cash contribution rather than a declared distribution. It remains in the same broad discounted-issuance cluster, so no multiplicity reset or independence claim is allowed.

facts: Optional cash investments range from $100 to $5,000 per month absent waiver.
Plan Agent must receive cash no later than two business days before the monthly investment date for purchase on the next succeeding purchase date.
Direct issuance occurs when shares trade at a premium to NAV; discount branch uses open-market purchases.
Direct-issue price is the greater of NAV or 95% of market price at the stated fixing.
Agent sale can deduct a $15 transaction fee plus $0.05 per share.
